summary: BLUT and Katana process adapters are merged into OpenWarrant; Katana native receipt interfaces merged upstream at 5a735133 with all hosted checks passing. A candidate core collector enrollment codec checks exact current authority, human-admin signature policy, executable/provider identity and explicit Warrant scope. Eight synthetic-adapter controls and 705 core regressions pass. Protected cryptographic enrollment workflow, operator custody, activation, native collector wiring and independent/participant qualification remain open. A candidate reference OpenSSH transport verifies exact enrollment bytes; four crypto/SDK controls, 17 process regressions and all-target/all-feature CLI Clippy pass, with two native-provider cases explicitly not run in this observation. Protected activation and collector wiring remain open. The candidate execution loader checks actual UID and protected paths, authenticates enrollment, and rechecks authority per use. Three loading controls, four crypto controls, an authority CLI regression, an explicitly run two-UID namespace roundtrip and strict CLI Clippy pass. Core enrollment is merged at d05cf826 after the full CI gate. Activation, native collector wiring, launch fencing and operator/independent qualification remain open. Prospective v2 authority activation now checks current human signer kind and current presence policy; retained history remains unchanged. Nine SDK authority controls, 707 core tests, three authority CLI unit tests and strict all-target/all-feature SDK/CLI Clippy pass. These software fixtures do not establish operator deployment or human review. The focused authentication plant passes 28 checks, including refusal of ordinary-signature presence downgrade. Eight integration regressions and a provisioned two-UID roundtrip pass; the initial default-scratch namespace failure is retained separately.
next_steps: Finish protected collector enrollment proposal/signing/activation transport; callable verification and read-only loading do not authenticate the acting collector or fence a native launch.
Wire trusted collector policy and native verifier into the actual workflow request/response path; preserve UNKNOWN for absent custody, spend or confinement observations.
Complete actual provider integrations, independent verification and participant qualification without inventing acceptance.
